gegevens.voet: In a sheet you can use these names directly, for example {{voorbeeld1}} or {{voorbeeld2}}. A sheet that assigns the name itself overrides the project value for that sheet only.

eenheden.label: Unit system
eenheden.hint: Every value is shown in the unit of its quantity, also in the bundled modules and on paper. Only the display changes: results and unity checks stay the same.

rekenwijze.label: Calculation method where the reference program differs
rekenwijze.hint: The reference calculation is the calculation program we use today and is therefore the default; every result can be checked against reference sheets. The standard mode follows the Eurocode itself at the marked points — that branch cannot be checked against a reference and is there for the moment this program stands on its own. The chosen answer is always shown on the printout.

CC.label: Consequence class
CC.hint: Determines K_FI (table B3, with the note to table NB.4 – A1.2(B)): CC1 → 0,90 · CC2 → 1,00 · CC3 → 1,10. Every sheet receives both CC and K_FI.

DesignLife.label: Design working life
DesignLife.hint: Minimum values according to table NB.1 – 2.1. A temporary structure falls in class 3, unless it is in use for at most 5 years (class 1) or has a use from class 2. The loads are calculated with a reference period of at least 15 years.

opties.5: 5 years — class 1: temporary, in use for at most 5 years
opties.15: 15 years — class 2: agricultural, industrial with 1 or 2 storeys
opties.50: 50 years — class 3: buildings and common structures (default)

windgebied.label: Wind zone
windgebied.hint: Zoning according to 4.2(1) note 2 of the NB, v_b0 from table NB.1: provincial boundaries, and in Noord-Holland a horizontal line at 52½° north; zone I is Noord-Holland above it (including Den Helder, Alkmaar, Hoorn, Heemskerk, Purmerend). Within 5 km of a boundary, v_b0 changes gradually (figure NB.1); the zone in which the location lies is then on the safe side. A sheet with wind load calculates q_p from this, using the reference height from the sheet.

opties.1: I — Wadden Islands, Wadden Sea, IJsselmeer, Markermeer and northern Noord-Holland (v_b0 = 29,5 m/s)
opties.2: II — rest of Noord-Holland, mainland Groningen and Friesland, Flevoland, Zuid-Holland, Zeeland (27,0)

terreincategorie.label: Terrain category
terreincategorie.hint: Follows from the surroundings of the building (Table NB.3-4.1).

tw_klasse.label: Building use category
tw_klasse.hint: Seismic importance factor I (building technical regulations, structures, art. 43-1 and seismic code 2.8): category 1 → 1.5 · 2 → 1.5 · 3 → 1.25 · 4 → 1.0. Wind importance factor I (wind code 2.5): categories 1–3 → 1.1 · 4 → 1.0. Every sheet receives tw_I and tw_Iw. The classification lists in the codes decide; the area thresholds for category 3 are in the code text. The wind code's temporary-structure class (I = 0.9) is not offered here.

opties.1: Category 1 — must stay operational after the event (government emergency offices, fire/police/telecom, evacuation schools, hospitals, power and water plants)
opties.2: Category 2 — storage of large quantities of toxic or explosive materials
opties.3: Category 3 — places where crowds gather (above the area thresholds of the code)

tw_DesignLife.label: Design working life (information)
tw_DesignLife.hint: Information for the print header only: the Taiwan modules do not calculate with it. The wind code relates importance to the return period (25 / 50 / 100 years); see the building use category for the factor that is actually used.

tw_terrein.label: Terrain category (wind code)
tw_terrein.hint: Terrain categories of the building wind code 2.3. The wind exponent α is derived (A 0.32 · B 0.25 · C 0.15). The gradient height z_g is only recorded for category C (300 m); for A and B it is 0, and the wind-load sheet then refuses to calculate until it is entered in the sheet from table 2.2. Intermediate terrain: use the category that gives the larger wind force.

opties.1: A — centre of a large city, at least 50% of the buildings higher than 20 m
opties.2: B — suburbs, small towns, scattered obstacles of 10–20 m
opties.3: C — flat open terrain, grassland, coast or lake shore (default)

tw_V10.label: Basic design wind speed V10(C) (m/s)
tw_V10.hint: 10-minute mean wind speed, terrain C, 10 m height, 50-year return period (wind code 2.4). Pick a district below for the suggested value, or type the value. A new wind-load sheet starts from this value when you changed it; an existing sheet keeps its own V_10.

tw_SDS.label: Site short-period design spectral acceleration S_DS
tw_SDS.hint: Seismic code 2.5 (S_DS = F_a·S_S^D; Taipei basin from 2.7). Depends on district, soil and near-fault distance: use the seismic-load sheet's helper for the exact value. A new seismic-load sheet starts from this value when you changed it.

tw_SD1.label: Site 1-second design spectral acceleration S_D1
tw_SD1.hint: Seismic code 2.5 (S_D1 = F_v·S_1^D; Taipei basin from 2.7). Same remarks as S_DS.
